title: Positivity conjecture for trigonometric polynomials from square-root coefficients
statement:
For $d\geq 2$, define the coefficients $b_k^{(d)}$ by

$$
\sqrt{1+z+\cdots+z^d}=\sum_{k=0}^\infty b_k^{(d)}z^k.
$$

For each $n\geq 0$, define the trigonometric polynomial

$$
\mathcal T_n^{(d)}(t)=\sum_{k=0}^n b_k^{(d)}\cos kt.
$$

**Positivity conjecture.** For $d\geq 2$, the trigonometric polynomials $\mathcal T_n^{(d)}(t)$ are positive for every $t\in\mathbb R$. Positivity of these polynomials is suggested as an approach to the zero-free Taylor polynomial conjecture and concerns the coefficients of the non-hypergeometric power series arising from $\sqrt{(1-z^{d+1})/(1-z)}$.
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2008–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2110.11549](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.11549), [arXiv:0806.3046](https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.3046).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.04544

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2025).
source_name: Leonid V. Kovalev, “Sharp bounds for some segments of bounded power series”, arXiv:2507.04544 (2025).
